questions.question: Which of the following is the longest tributary of the Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Yamuna, about 1,376 km long, is the longest tributary of the Ganga. It joins the Ganga at Prayagraj (Triveni Sangam). The Gandak, Ghaghara and Son are also Ganga tributaries but shorter.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India can the President's Rule be imposed in a state?
questions.explanation: Article 356 provides for the imposition of President's Rule in a state on the report of the Governor or otherwise. Article 352 deals with National Emergency, Article 360 with Financial Emergency and Article 368 with amendment of the Constitution.

questions.question: Kuchipudi, one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originates from which state?
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi takes its name from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh and is that state's classical dance form, blending dance, drama and song.

questions.question: Who founded the city of Jaipur in 1727?
questions.explanation: Sawai Jai Singh II, the Kachhwaha ruler of Amber, founded Jaipur in 1727, shifting his capital from Amber. He was also an astronomer who built the Jantar Mantar observatories.

questions.question: The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: The Concurrent List (subjects on which both the Union and states can legislate) is drawn from the Australian Constitution. Ireland inspired the Directive Principles, and Canada inspired the strong federal scheme.

questions.question: M. S. Swaminathan, who was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024, is best known as the architect of which movement in India?
questions.explanation: M. S. Swaminathan, the agricultural scientist behind the development of high-yielding varieties and the Green Revolution in India, was posthumously conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2024. The White Revolution is associated with Verghese Kurien.

questions.question: The Ninth Schedule, which protects certain laws from judicial review, was added to the Indian Constitution by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The Ninth Schedule was inserted by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, primarily to protect land reform laws from challenge. The 42nd Amendment added words like 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble, not the Ninth Schedule.

questions.question: Which country was the official host of the ICC Champions Trophy 2025?
questions.explanation: Pakistan was the official host of the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 (February-March 2025), its first global ICC event in nearly three decades; some matches, including India's games, were played in Dubai under the hybrid model.

questions.question: Which year was declared by the United Nations as the International Year of Millets, on India's proposal?
questions.explanation: The United Nations General Assembly, at India's initiative, declared 2023 the International Year of Millets (IYM 2023) to promote awareness and production of nutri-cereals.

questions.question: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is jointly hosted by which three countries, making it the first World Cup with three host nations?
options: A) United States, Brazil and Mexico
B) United States, Canada and Mexico
questions.explanation: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is jointly hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico - the first edition with 48 teams and the first with three co-hosts. The Spain-Portugal-Morocco bid relates to the 2030 World Cup.

questions.question: Which country held the chairmanship of BRICS for the year 2025?
questions.explanation: Brazil assumed the BRICS chairmanship for 2025 and hosted the 17th BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro in July 2025. Russia chaired BRICS in 2024 (Kazan Summit), and India took over the chairmanship for 2026.

questions.question: Who won the men's singles title at the 2025 French Open?
questions.explanation: Carlos Alcaraz of Spain won the 2025 French Open men's singles title, defeating Jannik Sinner in an epic five-set final, and successfully defended his Roland Garros crown.

questions.question: Which film won the Best Feature Film award at the 70th National Film Awards, announced in August 2024?
questions.explanation: At the 70th National Film Awards (announced in August 2024, for films certified in 2022), the Malayalam film 'Aattam' (The Play), directed by Anand Ekarshi, won the award for Best Feature Film. '2018' and 'Kantara' won honours in other categories.

questions.question: Exercise MALABAR 2024, the quadrilateral naval exercise involving India, the USA, Japan and Australia, was hosted by India at which city in October 2024?
questions.explanation: The 28th edition of Exercise MALABAR was hosted by India at Visakhapatnam in October 2024, with participation from the Indian Navy, the US Navy, the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force and the Royal Australian Navy.

questions.question: Speedometer : Speed :: Odometer : ?
questions.explanation: A speedometer measures speed; analogously, an odometer is the instrument that records the total distance travelled by a vehicle.

questions.question: Pointing to a man, Meera said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is Meera related to the man?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of Meera's mother is Meera herself. So the man's mother is Meera, i.e. Meera is the man's mother.

questions.question: Find the odd one out: 361, 441, 561, 625
questions.explanation: 361 = 19 squared, 441 = 21 squared and 625 = 25 squared are all perfect squares, while 561 is not a perfect square (23 squared = 529, 24 squared = 576). Hence 561 is the odd one out.

questions.question: Complete the letter series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.explanation: The gaps between successive letters increase by one each time: A(+2)C(+3)F(+4)J(+5)O(+6)? So the next letter is O + 6 = U.

questions.question: In a certain code, MANGO is written as PHOBN. How will APPLE be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter of MANGO is shifted one step forward (MANGO -> NBOHP) and the resulting string is written in reverse order (PHOBN). Applying the same rule to APPLE: shift each letter forward to get BQQMF, then shift-and-reverse gives FMQQB.

questions.question: If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, ... and so on, what word is represented by the code 3-15-14-20-18-15-12?
questions.explanation: Decoding each number to its alphabet position: 3=C, 15=O, 14=N, 20=T, 18=R, 15=O, 12=L, which spells CONTROL.

questions.question: Rohan starts from his house and cycles 6 km towards the east to reach a park. From the park he turns 90 degrees to his right and cycles 8 km to reach a library. From the library he turns 90 degrees to his right again and cycles 6 km to reach a bank. Finally, he turns 90 degrees to his left and cycles 3 km to reach the coaching centre. How far and in which direction is the coaching centre from his house?
questions.explanation: Taking the house as the origin and east as positive x: cycling 6 km east reaches (6, 0). A right turn points him south, so after 8 km he is at (6, -8). A second right turn points him west, so after 6 km he is at (0, -8). From the westward direction, a left turn points him south, so after 3 km he is at (0, -11). The coaching centre is 11 km due south of the house.

questions.question: Find the next term of the series: 2, 4, 9, 28, 125, ?
questions.explanation: Each term follows the pattern n! + n: 1! + 1 = 2, 2! + 2 = 4, 3! + 3 = 9, 4! + 4 = 28, 5! + 5 = 125. The next term is 6! + 6 = 720 + 6 = 726.

questions.question: The price of sugar increases by 25%. By what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that the expenditure on sugar remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: Required reduction = [increase / (100 + increase)] x 100 = (25/125) x 100 = 20%.

questions.question: How many numbers between 100 and 300 are exactly divisible by 7?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 7 between 100 and 300 run from 105 to 294. Their count is (294 - 105)/7 + 1 = 189/7 + 1 = 27 + 1 = 28.

questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 15. If the numbers 10 and 14 are excluded, what is the average of the remaining 6 numbers?
questions.explanation: Total of the 8 numbers = 8 x 15 = 120. Excluding 10 and 14 removes 24, leaving 96. The average of the remaining 6 numbers = 96/6 = 16.

questions.question: A car covers the first half of the distance between two towns at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: For equal distances, the average speed is the harmonic mean of the two speeds: (2 x 40 x 60)/(40 + 60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h. Taking the simple mean 50 km/h is the classic error.

questions.question: A alone can complete a piece of work in 15 days and B alone in 12 days. They work together for 4 days, after which B leaves. In how many days in total is the work finished?
questions.explanation: Let the work be 60 units (LCM of 15 and 12). A does 4 units/day and B does 5 units/day, so together 9 units/day. In 4 days they complete 36 units, leaving 24 units. A alone needs 24/4 = 6 days more. Total = 4 + 6 = 10 days.

questions.question: A trader sells two fans for Rs 1,800 each. On one he gains 20% and on the other he loses 20%. What is his overall result on the two transactions combined?
questions.explanation: Cost of the first fan = 1800/1.2 = Rs 1,500; cost of the second fan = 1800/0.8 = Rs 2,250. Total cost = Rs 3,750, while total selling price = Rs 3,600. Loss = Rs 150, i.e. 150/3750 x 100 = 4% loss.

questions.question: A person invests Rs 12,000 in a scheme A that offers simple interest at 8% per annum and Rs 8,000 in scheme B that offers simple interest at 6% per annum. After how many years will the difference between the interests earned from the two schemes be exactly Rs 4,320?
questions.explanation: Annual interest from A = 12000 x 8/100 = Rs 960; from B = 8000 x 6/100 = Rs 480. The annual difference is Rs 480, so the difference reaches Rs 4,320 after 4320/480 = 9 years.

questions.question: A vessel contains 40 litres of milk. 8 litres are drawn out and replaced with water, and this operation is performed once more. What is the ratio of milk to water in the vessel finally?
questions.explanation: After each replacement, milk remains (32/40) = 4/5 of its previous amount. Final milk = 40 x (4/5) x (4/5) = 25.6 litres, so water = 40 - 25.6 = 14.4 litres. Ratio = 25.6 : 14.4 = 16 : 9.

questions.question: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: Each interior angle of a regular n-sided polygon = (n - 2) x 180 / n. For n = 6: (4 x 180)/6 = 120 degrees.

questions.question: A ladder 25 m long leans against a vertical wall with its foot 7 m away from the base of the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, height = sqrt(25^2 - 7^2) = sqrt(625 - 49) = sqrt(576) = 24 m.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus are 12 cm and 16 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so each side = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 cm. Perimeter = 4 x 10 = 40 cm.

questions.question: In a survey of 400 students, 150 liked cricket, 120 liked football and 80 liked basketball, while the rest preferred tennis. If the data is shown in a pie chart, what is the central angle of the tennis sector?
questions.explanation: Students preferring tennis = 400 - (150 + 120 + 80) = 50. Central angle = (50/400) x 360 = 45 degrees.

questions.question: In a geometric progression, the 2nd term is 6 and the 5th term is 162. What is the common ratio?
questions.explanation: The 5th term divided by the 2nd term equals r^(5-2) = r^3. So r^3 = 162/6 = 27, giving r = 3.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x^4 + 1/x^4?
The sum of two positive numbers is 8 and their product is 12. What is the value of (sum of their squares) + (square of their product)?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be a and b. a^2 + b^2 = (a + b)^2 - 2ab = 64 - 24 = 40, and (ab)^2 = 12^2 = 144. Required value = 40 + 144 = 184.

questions.question: In a queue of students facing north, Kavya is 9th from the front end and 18th from the back end. How many students are standing ahead of the student who is exactly in the middle of the queue?
questions.explanation: Total students = 9 + 18 - 1 = 26. The middle positions are 13th and 14th, so the student exactly in the middle is the 13th. Students ahead of the 13th = 12.

questions.question: If the day before yesterday was Saturday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Day before yesterday = Saturday, so today = Monday. The day after tomorrow = Monday + 2 = Wednesday.

questions.question: Statements: All swimmers are athletes. Some chess players are swimmers. Conclusions: I. Some chess players are athletes. II. All athletes are chess players. Which conclusion(s) follow?
options: B) Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: The chess players who are swimmers must, by 'All swimmers are athletes', be athletes, so conclusion I follows. Conclusion II is the converse of the universal premise 'All swimmers are athletes'; a universal affirmative does not convert, so 'All athletes are chess players' does not follow.

questions.question: A clock seen through a mirror shows the time as 4:30. What is the actual time?
questions.explanation: A mirror image interchanges left and right on the clock face, so the actual time is obtained by subtracting the shown time from 11 hours 60 minutes: 11:60 - 4:30 = 7:30.

questions.question: Six friends - L, M, N, O, P and Q - sit around a circular table facing the centre. M sits second to the left of L. N sits opposite L. P sits immediately to the right of M. O does not sit adjacent to N. Who sits immediately to the left of O?
questions.explanation: For a person facing the centre, 'left' is the clockwise direction. Place L anywhere; two seats clockwise from L is M, and the seat opposite L is N. Immediately to the right of M means one seat anticlockwise from M, which is P. The two remaining seats are both adjacent to N, so O must take the one seat that is not adjacent to N, and Q takes the last seat. The clockwise neighbour of O, that is the person to O's immediate left, is L.

questions.question: Statement (advertisement): 'Use Shampoo X for dandruff-free hair.' Assumptions: I. People desire dandruff-free hair. II. No other shampoo can remove dandruff. Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
options: A) Neither I nor II is implicit
B) Both assumptions I and II are implicit
C) Only assumption II is implicit
D) Only assumption I is implicit
questions.explanation: An advertisement persuades by appealing to a felt desire, so assumption I is implicit. The advertisement does not claim exclusivity - it does not assert that no other shampoo removes dandruff - so II is not implicit.

questions.question: Four professionals - Nita, Om, Priya and Ravi - live in four different cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Kochi and Guwahati, and each practises a different profession: Doctor, Engineer, Teacher and Lawyer. (i) Nita lives in Delhi but is not the Doctor. (ii) The Engineer lives in Mumbai. (iii) The Doctor lives in Kochi. (iv) Priya is the Teacher. (v) Ravi is not the Engineer. (vi) The Doctor is not Om. Who among them is the Lawyer?
questions.explanation: Priya is the Teacher, so she cannot live in Mumbai (Engineer's city) or Kochi (Doctor's city); Delhi is Nita's, so Priya lives in Guwahati. Om and Ravi therefore live in Mumbai and Kochi. Since Ravi is not the Engineer, Ravi cannot be in Mumbai, so Ravi lives in Kochi and is the Doctor (consistent with 'Doctor is not Om'). Om lives in Mumbai and is the Engineer. Nita, in Delhi, is the remaining profession - the Lawyer - which also satisfies 'Nita is not the Doctor'.

questions.question: Deficiency of iodine in the human diet primarily causes which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Iodine is essential for the synthesis of thyroid hormones. Its deficiency causes enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as goitre; iodised salt is used to prevent it.

questions.question: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms an erect and diminished image and gives a wider field of view, enabling drivers to see more of the traffic behind; hence it is used as a rear-view mirror.

questions.question: Which acid is present in the gastric juice of the human stomach?
questions.explanation: Gastric juice contains hydrochloric acid (HCl), secreted by parietal cells of the stomach lining; it activates the enzyme pepsin and kills ingested microbes.

questions.question: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by which type of pathogen?
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which primarily attacks the lungs and spreads through airborne droplets.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration and produce most of the cell's ATP, the energy currency; hence they are called the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.question: Photochemical smog, common in large cities during sunny weather, is formed when certain primary pollutants react in sunlight with volatile organic compounds. Which of the following are the primary oxides responsible for it?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen oxides (especially NO2) react in sunlight with volatile organic compounds to form ozone, PAN and other secondary pollutants that make up photochemical smog. Sulphur oxides are associated with classical (London-type) smog instead.
